doc.title: Ira Gitler interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Researching documentary scripts on Armstrong and Hampton
summary: Gitler explains his research approach and the value of talking to living musicians like Milt Hinton and Doc Cheatham.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Two things real fast, real fast. You’re doing some work, being asked to provide information for scripts for a documentary is that right? On Louis and on Hamp?
No, I did that years ago.
Okay, tell us how that was for you, you know, providing the facts — helping to provide the facts for a documentary like that.

Well I just did my research, you know, starting with my own experience, my own knowledge of it up to that point, and then you just delve in and read as much as you can and if you’re able to talk to some of the musicians who were there, I think that’s very important. We have some great sources of information and expertise, people that were actually there and did it who are still alive. Milt Hinton and Doc Cheatham and people like this, who can tell us things that we don’t know first hand. Just as I can tell things first-hand because I was there at a certain time in the history of the music. And so whenever you can avail yourselves of the actual musicians, I think it’s very important to do that.
